Lead evidence update (reply to #9): I verified the reported class suffix against the pinned Sponge Mixin 0.17.5 bytecode. `InnerClassGenerator.getUniqueReference` explicitly replaces numeric inner suffixes with `Anonymous` and builds generated names as `<target>$<inner>$<UUID-without-dashes>`. That matches `ChiseledBookShelfBlockEntity$Anonymous$6b8fabc9a3dd3f94be74f1199f97fdb5`. The pinned client jar contains only ChiseledBookShelfBlockEntity.class, and the original BlockEntityTypes callsite points to the ordinary ChiseledBookShelfBlockEntity constructor; thus this is strong evidence of a Mixin-generated inner class requested while loading transformed code, not a vanilla jar omission. A plain method-reference probe on the current JDK yields Main$$Lambda/0x..., a different naming pattern. Need trace which mixin owns the generated inner class and provide Knot's class-generation behavior to J2H's loader before designing a fix.

Confirmed this class is generated by Sponge Mixin, not absent vanilla content. The official pinned client.jar has only ChiseledBookShelfBlockEntity.class; BlockEntityTypes uses an invokedynamic constructor reference to that class. Sponge Mixin 0.17.5 InnerClassGenerator bytecode converts numeric inner names such as $1 to Anonymous and forms target$Anonymous$UUID-without-dashes using UUID.nameUUIDFromBytes(originalName UTF-8). Fabric API nested fabric-transfer-api-v1 jar contains ChiseledBookShelfBlockEntityMixin$1.class, the source inner class. J2H transforms the host through AppClassLoader instrumentation, but the later generated-name request has no classpath resource; ordinary ClassFileTransformer cannot manufacture bytes for an absent resource during BuiltinClassLoader lookup. J2HFabricLauncher currently targets the system loader and provides only ordinary resource lookup.

Knot behavior and integration conclusion: pinned KnotClassDelegate.getPostMixinClassByteArray first gets the raw class bytes. For an absent generated class the bytes are null, and Knot still calls IMixinTransformer.transformClassBytes(name, name, null). Pinned MixinTransformer.transformClassBytes dispatches null input to generateClass(currentEnvironment, name), which routes through MixinClassGenerator and registered IClassGenerator implementations including InnerClassGenerator. Knot then defines the returned byte array through its ClassLoaderAccess.defineClassFwd(name, bytes, 0, len, codeSource). KnotClassLoader itself delegates loadClass/findClass to KnotClassDelegate; this is the essential generated-class path. J2H bypasses that path: Instrumentation sees only already-resolved classfile bytes, while BuiltinClassLoader cannot load a missing Mixin synthetic class from the JVM class path. Smallest plausible J2H patch without replacing the current system loader: after Mixin transforms a host, inspect its transformed NestMembers (InnerClassGenerator registers generated nest members); for each name recognized by transformer.getExtensions().getSyntheticClassRegistry().findSyntheticClass(name), request bytes using the same public IMixinTransformer.transformClassBytes(name,name,null) call Knot uses; create a small one-shot temp JAR containing those entries and call Instrumentation.appendToSystemClassLoaderSearch before returning host bytes. Do not mutate/reuse an already appended JAR; append one new completed archive per batch and retain its JarFile. Filter through synthetic registry rather than assuming every NestMember is generated. This is a viable parity shim, but depends on Instrumentation append support in the actual system loader and can hit package sealing/code-source differences; a target ClassLoader with a findClass fallback mirroring Knot is architecturally cleaner and avoids appending generated classes to the global loader. The minimum regression should use the real pinned fabric-transfer module and Minecraft 26.3 classes: transform ChiseledBookShelfBlockEntity with that mixin, then initialize BlockEntityTypes and assert its CHISELED_BOOKSHELF supplier can instantiate without NCDFE. Add a fixture Mixin with an anonymous inner class to prove hash-name generation and synthetic class resolution independent of Minecraft. No files changed.

Candidate caveat: generated classes loaded from the appended JAR will themselves pass through the installed Instrumentation transformers with non-null bytes, whereas Knot returns generated bytes directly from transformClassBytes(null) and then defines those bytes. Track synthetic names generated by this path and bypass the Mixin transformer for those names to avoid treating generated output as a fresh ordinary target; validate whether the AW transformer should also bypass them. Package sealing and adding a class into an already-defined JVM package from a different appended JAR need an explicit regression on the real JDK 26 system loader. This makes append-to-system-search viable for a first fix, but not equivalent to Knot unless those differences are covered.

Recommendation: approve the temporary-JAR bridge as a bounded compatibility patch for the verified blocker, but do not treat it as Knot-equivalent. Knot’s path is authoritative: when normal resource lookup returns null, Knot calls IMixinTransformer.transformClassBytes(name, name, null), allowing MixinClassGenerator and registered generators (including InnerClassGenerator) to return bytes, then defines those bytes in KnotClassLoader. The proposed call to generateClass is sound only if it reaches this same configured generator path; use the already verified transformClassBytes(name, name, null) route or confirm the exact method is equivalent.

A plain constant-pool-name scan is a useful discovery aid, but should not be the eligibility rule. Descriptors and invokedynamic bootstrap metadata may encode a class name as UTF8 rather than a CONSTANT_Class entry, and scanning can miss names or pick unrelated references. Prefer transformed NestMembers plus Mixin’s synthetic-class registry lookup; only append entries for names confirmed synthetic and successfully generated. If scanning remains necessary, parse all constant-pool UTF8 descriptors and structural attributes, and test invokedynamic/anonymous references.

The ordering is sound for the observed failure: generate and stage the synthetic bytes after Mixin has transformed the host, append the completed JAR before returning host bytes, and retain the JarFile for the JVM lifetime. That makes the missing resource visible to the current AppClassLoader before the host is defined or initialized. Guard against transforming a generated class a second time in the instrumentation callback, and ensure the generated entry name matches the requested binary name exactly. A single persistent/generated-class archive or batched immutable archives is safer than many one-class JARs; never rewrite an archive already passed to appendToSystemClassLoaderSearch. Validate system-loader support and make append/write errors fatal and visible, rather than returning host bytes with an unresolved reference.

Limits versus Knot: this is a global system-classloader resource workaround, not a loader-level findClass implementation. It does not reproduce Knot’s generated-class code source/ProtectionDomain, per-loader isolation, raw resource lookup, remapping, launch plugins, or general null-byte generation for classes not discovered in a transformed host. It may also be wrong if J2H later uses a non-system target loader. A full KnotClassLoader path is architecturally cleaner and needed for broad Fabric parity, but is a larger integration involving Knot launch lifecycle, classpath/resource routing and mapping setup. For the current one-JVM prototype, the append shim is a reasonable minimal step if constrained and documented.

Review of the current direct-definition implementation and evidence (read-only). ProtectionDomain/signers: code calls ClassLoader#defineClass(name, bytes, ..., hostDomain), so generated classes inherit the host class protection domain instead of getting a temporary JAR code source. The pinned 26.3 client JAR is signed (jarsigner reports Mojang signing; verification confirms signed entries). The immediately preceding temporary-JAR live run failed with a concrete signer mismatch for the bookshelf generated class. The newer direct-define run logs three “defined 1 Mixin-generated class(es)” and gets through startup without signer/package SecurityException, which is strong evidence the host-domain fix works on this signed client and OpenJDK 26.0.2.1. Knot’s pinned path derives CodeSource from the class source metadata and passes that CodeSource when defining both normal and generated classes; passing the host ProtectionDomain is directionally correct for an inner class belonging to that host source, but exact CodeSource/certificates and protection-domain permissions should be asserted in a focused test.

Nestmates/definition order: code parses transformed NestMembers, filters through Mixin synthetic registry, generates the null-input transform output, then defines synthetic members in the same loader and domain before returning host bytes. This matches the reported error path and the direct live run now reaches world startup. JVM nest membership is loader/package based and reciprocal metadata can resolve after the host is defined; predefinition is not rejected in the live JDK run. However, the log records only counts, not class names, and there is no explicit assertion that the bookshelf synthetic member loaded and the Chiseled bookshelf supplier instantiated. Current fixture source includes an anonymous class inside TargetMixin; it asserts the changed value after transformation, but does not assert nest metadata, class protection domain/signers, multiple nested levels, or definition-before-host behavior directly.

Instrumentation/module access: premain opens java.base/java.lang to the agent module with Instrumentation.redefineModule, then reflectively accesses protected ClassLoader#defineClass. This is narrowly scoped to java.lang, uses supported Instrumentation APIs, and empirically succeeds on the JDK 26 live run. It is still privileged JVM-wide access and requires agent instrumentation/module redefinition; unsupported/security-restricted JVM launch modes fail early. There is no fallback, which is preferable to pretending the define path works. Add a focused error assertion for unavailable redefine/open access and verify the documented minimum Java runtime.

Exception reporting: transform/generation/definition failures are caught as Throwable, saved in one volatile mixinTransformFailure string, logged, and the callback returns null. Lifecycle polls this only after Minecraft client bootstrap. Thus one failure can silently cause original host bytes to be defined and later concurrent failures overwrite the diagnostic; failures after this one startup polling boundary are not surfaced to Rust. This remains a correctness issue despite the improvement over stderr-only. Keep an accumulated thread-safe list or fail the owning startup path, and test both a thrown transformer error and a generated-class define error. Do not overstate per-mod isolation: Mixin transformations are global pre-entrypoint work and are not attributed to registration transactions.

Concurrency: synchronization on the Mixin transformer serializes transformation and synthetic definition; generated names use a concurrent set, while local pending/visited/generated collections are per invocation. That prevents duplicate generation through this path, but no concurrent class-load regression exists. Because the global Mixin monitor is held while invoking a reflective defineClass that can trigger verifier/class loading and nested transformer callbacks, add concurrent target loads that reference shared/nested generated classes and verify there is no deadlock or duplicate definition. The repeated current log counts do not constitute a race test.

Reply to #24: verified against the current 16:13 agent jar/source (direct ClassLoader.defineClass variant), not the superseded append-JAR variant.

1) Real pinned Fabric Transfer API + Minecraft 26.3: /tmp/j2h-anon RealHarness registers fabric-transfer-api-v1-8.0.25, calls FabricLoaderBootstrap.initializeMixins("client"), then MinecraftBootstrap.install() against the signed client-26.3.jar. Result: Mixin transformed ChiseledBookShelfBlockEntity; J2H defined 1 Mixin-generated class(es); MinecraftBootstrap OK, version=26.3. No NCDFE, no SecurityException. So direct definition with the host ProtectionDomain works on JDK 26 in both JNI_CreateJavaVM and plain java.

2) Knot comparison: KnotClassDelegate.getMetadata(name) returns Metadata.EMPTY when getResource(name.class) is null; Metadata.EMPTY has null CodeSource. defineClassFwd is then called with a null CodeSource, not the host ProtectionDomain. So J2H host-domain reuse is a deliberate deviation, not Knot parity. It is necessary here because the pinned client-26.3.jar is Mojang-signed: a generated class with no certs in a signed package throws SecurityException (checkCerts), which I reproduced with the superseded append-JAR path. Current host-domain variant avoids that. In Fabric production the Minecraft jar is remapped/unsigned, so Knot null CodeSource is consistent. Keep the comment/docs clear that host-domain reuse is the signed-jar adaptation.

3) Defining generated classes before the host is valid: I pre-defined the nested fixture generated class with reflective ClassLoader.defineClass before loading either host; later new Outer.Inner().value() returned 42. No definition-order problem observed. Current code defines during host transform before returning host bytes; that worked for top-level and nested-with-preloaded-outer.

4) Found a critical gap in the current NestMembers-only discovery. Reproducer /tmp/j2h-anon/nested: @Mixin(targets="fixture.Outer$Inner") with an anonymous Supplier; fresh JVM, no preload. Current agent logs "J2H: Mixin transformed fixture.Outer$Inner" then throws NoClassDefFoundError for fixture/Outer$Inner$Anonymous$9ded9fb2ec3a323e914b6716e1ccbe20. Reason: the generated class is registered as a nest member of Outer, not of the transformed target Inner; J2H only scans the transformed host NestMembers, and Outer is never transformed before Inner.<clinit> resolves the generated class. Preloading/transforming Outer first makes it pass (value=42), because Outer NestMembers then contains the generated name. This is a real nested-target/nest-host case, and also covers any config where no NestMembers are emitted.

5) Minimal fix direction validated partially: SyntheticClassRegistry.classes is already populated before target transform (size 1 immediately after initializeMixins; keys are internal names like fixture/Outer$Inner$Anonymous$<hash>). In defineGeneratedNestMembers, derive hostName from the transformed bytes and seed pending with registry keys whose dotted name starts with hostName + "$" (or whose InnerClassInfo target equals host), then generate/define with the current host domain. I manually enumerated that registry, generated the class and defined it before loading Inner; value=42. Adding that to the current NestMembers set should fix the nested fresh case without a loader rewrite. The fully general fallback is still a loader findClass that calls transformClassBytes(name,name,null) on miss, like Knot.

6) Constraints/risks to keep: reflective ClassLoader.defineClass after redefineModule(java.lang) works on JDK 26 but is JDK-sensitive; keep failures fatal; loader==null currently returns without defining, so bootstrap-loader targets would still fail; domain for generated classes must stay the host/package domain or signed packages fail; current synchronization on transformer is good; add a regression for the nested target case plus the real transfer case. I made no repo edits.

Read-only verification complete. Pinned Fabric Loader 0.20.1 Knot source/bytecode confirms: after getPostMixinClassByteArray returns generated bytes, tryLoadClass calls getMetadata(name), then ClassLoaderAccess.defineClassFwd(name, bytes, 0, len, metadata.codeSource). It does not reuse the transformed host ProtectionDomain. Because the generated binary name has no resource, getMetadata returns Metadata.EMPTY and null CodeSource. Also, pinned Knot getMetadata(Path) opens the JAR root connection and calls JarURLConnection.getCertificates() there; on the same JDK 26 and exact official client.jar this returns 0 certificates. Its intended per-entry signer extraction remains a TODO/commented block. Thus Knot currently assigns no JAR signer certificates even to ordinary client classes in this path. Direct J2H definition with the host ProtectionDomain is different but more consistent with its actual AppClassLoader: exact client.jar entry is signed (JarFile verification gave 4 certificates / 1 CodeSigner), and loading ChiseledBookShelfBlockEntity via URLClassLoader gave a ProtectionDomain CodeSource with one signer. Reusing host PD keeps generated and host class signers identical and avoids the JVM same-package signer mismatch a null/unsigned PD would cause on this signed JAR. It is a deliberate security-domain choice, not byte-for-byte Knot parity. Nest timing: on the installed OpenJDK 26.0.2, I defined a member class before its NestHost using ClassLoader#defineClass, then defined host; getNestHost returned the host and an instance method reading the host private field worked. The same succeeded for a non-static inner class with synthetic this$0 outer reference. So predefinition before host definition is valid for ordinary JVM nest attributes; transformed host must still include the member name, and both classes must use the same loader/package.
